_readme: Gameweeks a player was UNAVAILABLE for — injured, suspended, or not yet
signed. The FPL API records none of this historically, so the minutes
model divides starts by league gameweeks played and reads an injury
absence as a manager's decision to leave someone out.
This is data entry, not judgement: an absence is checkable against any
injury record. projections.py REFUSES an entry for a gameweek in which
the player actually logged minutes, so it cannot be used to inflate
It only ever shrinks the denominator — it cannot invent starts. A player
with one start in three available games still reads as a rotation risk,
just not as badly as one start in seven.
DELETE an entry once the absence is far enough back that it no longer
distorts the rate — roughly once he has as many available gameweeks as
he missed. A stale entry quietly flatters him forever.
Prefer player ids; ambiguous names are refused.
